scope: Bounded hosted Metal correctness and Linux ARM64 qualification. Test sets overlap and are not a combined case total or full release gate.

metal.subject: 391b6deed4f7ec106a904b8d634305a463ea90d0

defect.qualification: The same prior run also timed out; it was not a passing Intel qualification.

diagnosis.subject: c6537971da4c08cbaf19ef03d1a3ad6c5f229668
diagnosis.method: Five generated sum-loop variants, three fast-math settings and two dispatch group sizes, retaining exact input/output comparisons.
diagnosis.interpretation: Evidence supports a loop-state optimization problem on this hosted runtime, not a general proof of a Metal driver defect. Formula control was diagnostic only and is not the retained lowering.

metal.change: Use volatile storage for scalar Metal fold/loop state, preserving ordinary C output and all actual iterations. Separate cache identities prevent reuse across storage modes. Check Metal command completion before consuming output.

outputSize.method: Identical input IR; generated Metal source bytes before and after the lowering change.

limitations: No Metal performance or energy comparison; volatile storage may carry runtime cost.
Experimental compiler/emit_metal.a0 is a separate non-production route and is not changed by this host-emitter fix.
Hosted focused, behavior and corpus case sets overlap.

linuxArm64.subject: 08217de0f895114ac20fd07efe24ed4327c92677
linuxArm64.acceptance: Existing corpus, hardware, .NET and Life commands passed. This result predates the Metal fix and does not qualify another tree.

pendingIntelUnit.subject: df00c49460defed404fd71eec26d906d65767cca
pendingIntelUnit.method: Two disjoint exhaustive file partitions, with unchanged test commands and per-job limits. Aggregate fails unless both succeed.

release: Full release, physical devices, independent AI study, native cost acceptance and protection assurance remain outstanding.
